subject: questions about model averaging with multi species model

messages.author: 7eed7eee7dd92cf3
messages.subject: questions about model averaging with multi species model
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I am using the multi species model to investigate occupancy of 4 species, 2 of them (species 1 and species 3) with relatively few detections compared to the other species.

I am interested in modelling the relationships, if any, between pair of species (e.g. 1 vs 2 and 3 vs 4), and I have hence constrained the parameters for the remaining interacting states to 0.

Only 2 models are supported by the data among the set of candidate models, the first one includes the interaction between species 1 and 2 with one covariate, while the second one includes the interaction between species 3 and 4 with one covariate. 

When conducting model averaging using these two models with "mean" values for the covariates using the function modavgPred from the AICcmodavg package, I got the following output.
 
# Model-averaged predictions on the response scale
# based on entire model set and 95% confidence interval:
#
#             mod.avg.pred uncond.se lower.CL upper.CL
# psi[1111]-1        0.111     0.134   -0.152    0.375
# psi[1110]-1        0.006     0.030   -0.054    0.065
# psi[1101]-1        0.009     0.041   -0.071    0.090
# psi[1100]-1        0.009     0.040   -0.069    0.087
# psi[1011]-1        0.007     0.016   -0.024    0.039
# psi[1010]-1        0.000     0.002   -0.004    0.005
# psi[1001]-1        0.001     0.003   -0.004    0.005
# psi[1000]-1        0.001     0.004   -0.007    0.008
# psi[0111]-1        0.643     0.233    0.187    1.100
# psi[0110]-1        0.035     0.063   -0.088    0.158
# psi[0101]-1        0.056     0.092   -0.124    0.236
# psi[0100]-1        0.054     0.098   -0.138    0.245
# psi[0011]-1        0.053     0.085   -0.115    0.220
# psi[0010]-1        0.004     0.013   -0.021    0.029
# psi[0001]-1        0.006     0.028   -0.049    0.061
# psi[0000]-1        0.006     0.027   -0.047    0.058

Now the questions:

1) from the output it appears (to me) that only the interaction between 3 species (species 2, 3, 4) is significant, given that 0 is not included in the 95% CI. 

Am I wrong? 

2) I was not expecting to see the predictions for those occupancy states which were set to 0 in the models.

Should I do something different to get model averaged predictions given the structure of the models (i.e. interactions only between pair of species) ? 

Stef

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] questions about model averaging with multi species model
parts:
Hi Stefano,

Regarding the format of the output for the occuMulti model type,
modavgPred( ) calls the predict( ) function which gives you predicted
values of psi for all the combinations of species presence and absence.
Note that exceptionally for this model type, the confidence intervals
are computed directly on the probability scale: this is why you are
getting intervals that extend below 0 and above 1. One of these
intervals excludes 0, but this is just reflecting that the precision on
the estimate is higher than for the others, not necessarily that the
species interaction is "significant".

If you want to determine how the probability of a given state (e.g.,
[1100]) changes with a given explanatory variable across your models,
then you could supply a vector of values for one explanatory variable
of interest and hold the other explanatory variables constant. You
could then extract the predicted probabilities for the state of
interest and plot it on a graph against the vector of values of the
explanatory variable. For example, if you have a vector of 30 values,
you would extract rows psi[1100]-1, psi[1100]-2, psi[1100]-3, ...,
psi[1100]-30 to include in your plot.

Hope it helps,

Marc
